title: Westerlund 2 through Webb’s eyes
caption: The star cluster Westerlund 2 in the star-forming region Gum 29, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: Westerlund 2, Gum 29 · constellation Carina · about 20,000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, V. Almendros-Abad, M. Guarcello, K. Monsch, and the EWOCS team

recognition.text: ESA/Webb Picture of the Month, December 2025 (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Thousands of stars glitter above walls of glowing orange and red gas in this festive-looking Webb view. At the top shines Westerlund 2, a young cluster about 20,000 light-years away in Carina, the Keel, inside the star-forming region Gum 29.

The cluster holds some of the hottest, brightest and most massive stars in the Milky Way, and their strong light shapes everything around them. Below and around them, the gas forms carved walls and knotted clouds, eroded and lit by the cluster’s radiation. Small, newly igniting stars are scattered throughout, some still wrapped in the gas and dust they formed from, while soft blue and pink tones mark thinner material between the denser clouds.

For the first time, Webb has revealed the full population of brown dwarfs in this very massive young cluster, down to about 10 times the mass of Jupiter. It is also helping astronomers find several hundred stars with discs at different stages, clues to how planets form.
scale: The cluster itself spans roughly 6 to 13 light-years, according to the release. Its light set out about 20,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Webb's NIRCam and MIRI in eleven infrared filters from 1.15 to 11 microns, shown from blue (shortest) through cyan, green and orange to red (longest).
understand.eye: All of this is infrared light, which the eye can’t see, so every color here is assigned.

explore: Westerlund 2 also starred in Hubble’s 25th-anniversary image in 2015. Webb sees it in infrared light, which passes through much of the dust that hides young stars in visible light. The data come from Webb’s EWOCS survey of the Westerlund 1 and 2 clusters.
alt: A bright cluster of young stars at top above sculpted orange and red clouds of gas, scattered with many small stars and soft blue and pink wisps.
